subject: Cognitive Science
title: Statistical Thinking
description: A short lesson to help you apply Statistical Thinking.

hook.text: A hospital has a cluster of five cancer cases. Alarmed? In a city of millions, clusters happen by chance alone.

buildup.text: Statistical thinking means evaluating evidence through probability rather than anecdote or intuition.

discovery.text: Humans see patterns in randomness. Flipping HHTHT feels more random than HHHHH—but they're equally likely.

twist.text: Regression to the mean fools everyone: a great quarter is followed by an average one, and we blame the decline.

climax.text: Learning base rates, sample size, and variance gives you a lens that most people lack entirely.

punchline.text: Think in probabilities, not in stories.

quiz.question: Why is statistical thinking a debiasing tool?
options: It evaluates evidence through probability, not intuition
